title: The Complete Mediterranean Cookbook
author: America's Test Kitchen
cuisine: mediterranean (entire book) - a loved cuisine; strong, reliable source (ATK kitchen-tested)
note: Catalog built from chapter recipe-list pages (titles + page numbers). To add any as a real cookwhat recipe, scan the full recipe page for the ingredient list + method. PARTIAL: covers Rice & Grains (ch.4), Pasta & Couscous (ch.5), Vegetables (ch.7), Poultry/Pork/Lamb/Beef, Spice Blends & Pastes, Seafood (ch.8), Eggs (ch.10), Breads/Flatbreads/Pizzas (ch.11), and Fruit & Sweets (ch.12). Now also includes Meze/Antipasti/Small Plates (ch.1), Soups (ch.2), and Salads (ch.3) - essentially the full book. A 'Beans' chapter (if the book has one) may not be captured. A few lamb page numbers are best-effort.
source_format: Source for any meal cataloged from this book: "The Complete Mediterranean Cookbook (ATK) - p.NNN" (no URL).
dislikeFlags: Broccoli and Feta Frittata flagged (broccoli). White-bean/chickpea mains flagged (keep beans low). No curry dishes.

ingredients: 1 (14-oz) can whole peeled tomatoes, drained and chopped
2 hard-cooked large eggs, whites and yolks separated
steps: Heat oven to 300F. Pat the chicken dry, season, and brown in the oil ~3-4 min per side; transfer to a plate.
Soften the onions in the fat, then add garlic, bay leaf, and cinnamon ~30 sec. Add wine and tomatoes, return the chicken skin-side up, and braise in the oven until tender.
Make the picada: process the toasted almonds and the hard-cooked egg yolks with a little braising liquid into a paste.
Off heat, discard the bay leaf and stir the almond-yolk picada into the sauce to thicken; finish with lemon juice and half the parsley.
Chop the egg whites and sprinkle over the chicken with the remaining parsley.
tips: This is pollo en pepitoria - the sauce is thickened with a picada of ground toasted almonds + hard-cooked egg yolks, not flour.
Toast the almonds first for deeper flavor and grind the picada fine so the sauce is silky, not gritty.
It's rich and nutty - brighten at the end with lemon and parsley, and use the chopped egg whites as garnish.

recipes.title: Braised Chicken Thighs with Moroccan Pistachio and Currant Sauce
Roasted Chicken with Fennel, Olive, and Orange Sauce

ingredients: 1 whole chicken (3.5 to 4 lb), giblets discarded
steps: Combine the garlic heads, bay leaves, and 1/2 cup salt in a 1-gallon zipper-lock bag and crush gently with a rolling pin; transfer to a large container and stir in 2 quarts water to dissolve the salt. Butterfly the chicken: with it breast side down, use kitchen shears to cut along both sides of the backbone and discard it; trim excess fat and skin around the neck. Flip the chicken, open it up, and press to flatten. Submerge in the brine, cover, and refrigerate 1 hour.

Meanwhile, cook the oil, minced garlic, pepper flakes, and 2 teaspoons pepper in a small saucepan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Let the oil cool, then reserve 2 tablespoons for serving.

Remove the chicken from the brine and pat dry. Brush with the seasoned oil and grill, weighted with a foil-wrapped brick or Dutch oven, until the skin is browned and crisp and the meat is cooked through, turning as needed. Rest, then carve and serve drizzled with the reserved oil and lemon wedges.
tips: Butterfly (spatchcock) the chicken — removing the backbone and flattening it lets the bird cook quickly and evenly on the grill.
Brine for 1 hour for well-seasoned, juicy meat.
Weight the chicken with a foil-wrapped brick or Dutch oven on the grill for even contact, crisp skin, and good browning.
Blooming the garlic and pepper flakes in oil infuses the chicken with deep, devilish heat; reserve 2 tablespoons of that oil to drizzle at the table.
This dish runs very spicy — cut back the red pepper flakes for a milder version.

recipes.title: Grilled Chicken Kebabs with Tomato-Feta Salad

ingredients: 1 teaspoon grated lemon zest plus 3 tablespoons juice
1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Whisk oil, lemon zest and juice, garlic, oregano, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper together in medium bowl. Reserve half of oil mixture in second bowl. Add tomatoes, feta, and onion to remaining oil mixture and toss to coat; season and set aside for serving.
Whisk yogurt into reserved oil mixture. Set aside half of yogurt dressing for serving. Add chicken to remaining yogurt dressing and toss to coat. Thread chicken onto four 12-inch metal skewers.
Set up grill: charcoal — chimney of 6 quarts briquettes, pour evenly, grate on, covered 5 minutes; gas — all burners high, covered, 15 minutes, leave on high.
Grill skewers, turning occasionally, until chicken is well browned and registers 160 degrees, about 10 minutes. Slide chicken off skewers onto platter; serve with salad and reserved dressing.
tips: The yogurt marinade is the whole trick — it protects lean breast meat from drying out on the grill.
One dressing, three jobs: half dresses the tomato-feta salad, and the yogurt-enriched half splits again into marinade and finishing sauce.
You will need four 12-inch metal skewers.
The cherry tomato-feta-red onion salad is built into the recipe — it's what turns the kebabs into a full meal.

ingredients: 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for serving
4 red or yellow bell peppers, quartered, stemmed, seeded, and cut crosswise into 1/4-inch-wide strips
1 onion, quartered through root end and sliced crosswise into 1/4-inch-wide strips
6 garlic cloves, lightly crushed and peeled
2 tablespoons capers plus 4 teaspoons caper brine
steps: Combine oregano and 1 teaspoon salt in bowl. Cut steak with grain into 3 equal pieces. Sprinkle steak with oregano mixture, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 24 hours.

Heat 1/3 cup oil in 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking. Add bell peppers, onion, garlic, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are soft, about 10 minutes.

Stir in tomatoes and their juice, capers and brine, and pepper flakes and cook, uncovered, until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Transfer peperonata to bowl, cover, and keep warm.

Wipe skillet clean with paper towels. Pat steaks dry and season with pepper. Heat remaining 1 tablespoon oil in now-empty skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking. Cook steaks until well browned and meat registers 120 to 125 degrees (for medium-rare), 5 to 7 minutes per side. Transfer to carving board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 10 minutes.
Stir basil into peperonata. Slice steaks thin against grain on bias. Season slices with salt and pepper and drizzle with extra oil. Serve steak with peperonata.
tips: Cut the steak WITH the grain into 3 pieces for cooking, then slice thin AGAINST the grain on the bias to serve — that's what makes flank tender.
The oregano-salt rub can go on up to 24 hours ahead (minimum 30 minutes) — do it in the morning and the meat is fully seasoned by dinner.
Peperonata = peppers, onion, tomato, and garlic melted together in a hefty pour of olive oil; capers + brine give it the tang.
Pull the steak at 120-125 degrees for medium-rare and rest 10 minutes tented; there's a doneness chart on p.310.
The basil goes into the peperonata only while the meat rests, so it stays fresh; a final drizzle of olive oil balances the tangy, meaty flavors.

ingredients: 2 green Thai chiles, stemmed and chopped
steps: Microwave oil, coriander, cumin, cardamom, salt, and cloves in covered bowl until fragrant, about 30 seconds; let cool to room temperature.

Pulse oil-spice mixture, cilantro, parsley, chiles, and garlic in food processor until coarse paste forms, about 15 pulses, scraping down sides of bowl as needed. (Green Zhoug can be refrigerated for up to 4 days.)
tips: Tagged FAST + VEG. Zhoug is an Israeli hot sauce, red or green — the book likes this green version with fish or drizzled on sandwiches.
Blooming the ground spices in oil (30 seconds in the microwave) is what wakes them up before the herbs go in.
HEAT CONTROL: the 2 green Thai chiles make it properly spicy — for a mild build use 1 chile, seeded (or a seeded jalapeño), and always serve it on the side so everyone doses their own.
FOOD SAFETY (from the page's sidebar): pastes with raw garlic submerged in oil — zhoug, harissa — keep at most 4 DAYS refrigerated.

steps: Combine all ingredients in bowl and microwave until bubbling and very fragrant, about 1 minute, stirring halfway through microwaving; let cool to room temperature. (Harissa can be refrigerated for up to 4 days.)
tips: Tagged FAST + VEG. North African condiment for soups, sauces, dressings, or dolloped on lamb, hummus, eggs, sandwiches.
No Aleppo pepper? Substitute 3/4 teaspoon paprika + 3/4 teaspoon finely chopped red pepper flakes.
Raw-garlic-in-oil paste: at most 4 days refrigerated (page sidebar).

steps: Toast cardamom, coriander, cumin, anise, allspice, and peppercorns in small skillet over medium heat until fragrant, shaking skillet occasionally to prevent scorching, about 2 minutes. Let cool to room temperature.
Transfer toasted spices, ginger, nutmeg, Aleppo, and cinnamon to spice grinder and process to fine powder. (Can be stored at room temperature in airtight container for up to 1 year.)
tips: Tagged FAST + VEG. Complex Moroccan warm-spice blend — robust flavor for couscous dishes, soups, stews, braises.
No Aleppo? 1/2 teaspoon paprika + 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes.
Keeps a year at room temperature in an airtight container.

steps: Combine all ingredients in bowl. (Za'atar can be stored at room temperature in airtight container for up to 1 year.)
tips: Tagged FAST + VEG. Aromatic eastern Mediterranean blend used as seasoning AND condiment — sprinkle into olive oil as a bread dip, into grain dishes, or over hummus.
Three ingredients, no cooking; keeps a year airtight at room temperature.

steps: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 400 degrees. Pat chickpeas dry with paper towels and toss with oil. Spread into single layer on rimmed baking sheet and roast until browned and crisp, 40 to 45 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes; let cool completely.

Process chickpeas in food processor until coarsely ground, about 10 seconds; transfer to medium bowl. Pulse pistachios and sesame seeds in now-empty processor until coarsely ground, about 15 pulses; add to bowl. Process coriander, cumin, and fennel seeds until finely ground, 2 to 3 minutes; add to bowl. Add pepper and salt and whisk until well combined. (Dukkah can be refrigerated for up to 1 month.)
tips: Tagged VEG. North African blend of spices, nuts, and seeds — on olive oil as a bread dip, a crunchy coating for goat cheese, a soup garnish, or a topping for grain and bean salads.
The chickpea roast is the time sink: 40-45 minutes at 400 with stirring — make it AHEAD, not night-of.
Keeps up to 1 MONTH refrigerated, so a weekend batch covers many uses.
No chile heat in it at all — crunch and warm spice only.

steps: Combine all ingredients in bowl. (Can be stored at room temperature in airtight container for up to 1 year.)
tips: Tagged FAST + VEG. Aromatic dried-herb blend from the south of France — use as a rub for poultry or pork.
Keeps a year airtight at room temperature.

Spanish-Style Brothy Rice with Clams and Salsa Verde

ingredients: 1 pound extra-large shrimp (21 to 25 per pound), peeled and deveined
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra as needed
1 pound boneless, skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and halved crosswise
1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded, and cut into 1/2-inch-wide strips
8 ounces Spanish-style chorizo sausage, sliced on bias 1/2 inch thick
1 (14.5-ounce) can diced tomatoes, drained, minced, and drained again
steps: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and heat oven to 350 degrees. Toss shrimp with 1 tablespoon oil, 1 teaspoon garlic, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper; cover and refrigerate. Pat chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 teaspoons oil in Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Cook bell pepper until skin begins to blister and turn spotty black, about 4 minutes; transfer to bowl.

Heat remaining 1 teaspoon oil; brown chicken in single layer, about 3 minutes per side; transfer to bowl. Reduce heat to medium and cook chorizo, stirring frequently, until deeply browned and fat renders, about 5 minutes; transfer to bowl with chicken.

Add extra oil to fat in pot to equal 2 tablespoons. Cook onion until softened, about 3 minutes; stir in remaining garlic, 1 minute. Stir in tomatoes; cook until darkened and slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Stir in rice until grains are well coated, about 2 minutes.

Stir in broth, wine, saffron, bay leaf, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Return chicken and chorizo to pot, increase heat to medium-high, and bring to boil, stirring occasionally. Cover, transfer pot to oven, and bake until almost all liquid is absorbed, 15 to 20 minutes.

Remove pot. Scatter shrimp and mussels over rice, pushing hinge side of mussels into rice so they stand up. Cover, return to oven, and bake until shrimp are opaque and mussels have opened, 10 to 15 minutes.
For optional socarrat: transfer pot to stovetop, remove lid, and cook over medium-high heat about 5 minutes, rotating pot, until bottom layer of rice is well browned and crisp.
Discard unopened mussels and bay leaf. Arrange bell pepper strips in pinwheel over rice, sprinkle with peas, cover, and let sit 5 minutes. Sprinkle with parsley; serve with lemon wedges.
tips: A Dutch oven (at least 6 quarts) stands in for the paella pan — no specialty equipment.
Bomba rice is most traditional; any Valencia rice works, and Arborio is an acceptable substitute.
Dry-cured Spanish chorizo is the sausage of choice; fresh chorizo or linguica is an acceptable substitute.
Chicken broth, white wine, saffron, and a bay leaf are the whole seasoning backbone — don't overcomplicate.
Socarrat (the crusty browned rice layer) doesn't develop in the oven version — use the optional stovetop step 7 to make it before serving.
VARIATION — Indoor Paella in a Paella Pan: use a 14- to 15-inch pan, increase broth to 3 1/4 cups and wine to 1/2 cup, and cover tightly with foil before it goes in the oven.

ingredients: 1 1/2 teaspoons minced fresh thyme or 1/2 teaspoon dried
steps: Heat oil in large saucepan over medium heat until shimmering. Add onion and 1/2 teaspoon salt; cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in barley, garlic, and thyme and cook, stirring frequently, until barley is lightly toasted and fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Stir in water and bring to simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until barley is tender and water is absorbed, 20 to 40 minutes.
Off heat, lay clean dish towel underneath lid and let pilaf sit 10 minutes. Add parsley, chives, and lemon juice, fluff gently with fork, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
tips: Cooking time swings 20 to 40 minutes depending on how heavily the barley was pearled — the label won't tell you, so start checking at 20.
Do NOT substitute hulled, hull-less, quick-cooking, or presteamed barley.
Toasting the barley with the onion before adding water is what brings out the nuttiness.
The dish-towel-under-the-lid rest absorbs excess moisture; lemon juice at the end is the fresh finish.

ingredients: 3 tomatoes, cored and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
steps: Toss tomatoes with 1/4 teaspoon salt in fine-mesh strainer set over bowl and let drain, tossing occasionally, 30 minutes; reserve 2 tablespoons drained tomato juice. Toss bulgur with 2 tablespoons lemon juice and reserved tomato juice in bowl and let sit until grains begin to soften, 30 to 40 minutes.

Whisk remaining 2 tablespoons lemon juice, oil, cayenne, and 1/4 teaspoon salt together in large bowl. Add tomatoes, bulgur, parsley, mint, and scallions and toss gently to combine. Cover and let sit at room temperature until flavors have blended and bulgur is tender, about 1 hour. Before serving, toss to recombine and season with salt and pepper.
tips: Tagged VEG. No cooking at all — but budget ~2 hours of resting: 30 min tomato drain, 30-40 min bulgur soak, then 1 hour for the assembled salad.
Salting and draining the tomatoes keeps the salad from going soggy; the drained juice + lemon juice is what the bulgur soaks in (never plain water) — that's where the flavor comes from.
Two mild scallions, not chopped onion — onion overwhelmed the salad in testing.
Herbs and vegetables go in while the bulgur is still finishing, so everything mingles into one cohesive dish.
Use MEDIUM-GRIND BULGUR — do not confuse it with cracked wheat, which takes far longer and will not work here.
VARIATION on the same page: Spiced Tabbouleh (body not fully captured in this scan).

Orzo with Shrimp, Feta, and Lemon

ingredients: 1 tablespoon grated lemon zest plus 1 tablespoon juice
1 1/2 pounds extra-large shrimp (21 to 25 per pound), peeled and deveined
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for serving
1/2 cup pitted kalamata olives, chopped coarse
steps: Combine lemon zest, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper in medium bowl. Add shrimp, toss to coat, and refrigerate until ready to use.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, about 30 seconds. Add orzo and cook, stirring frequently, until coated with oil and lightly browned, about 5 minutes. Stir in broth and water and bring to boil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until orzo is al dente, about 6 minutes. Stir in olives, 1/4 cup feta, and lemon juice; season with salt and pepper.

Reduce heat to medium-low, nestle shrimp into orzo, cover, and cook until shrimp are opaque throughout, about 5 minutes. Sprinkle with parsley and remaining 1/4 cup feta and drizzle with extra oil. Serve.
tips: Toss the shrimp with salt, pepper, and lemon ZEST ahead — it infuses them with clean citrus flavor while they wait in the fridge.
Toasting the orzo (about 5 minutes, until lightly browned) deepens its flavor and coats each grain with oil so they stay separate and distinct.
Chicken broth (half the liquid) gives a more savory profile than water alone.
The shrimp cook through GENTLY, nestled into the finished orzo off a covered low heat — that's what keeps them tender, and it keeps the whole dish in one pan.
Kalamata olives are the briny counterpoint; the feta goes in twice — half stirred in, half sprinkled on top.

ingredients: 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (or unsalted butter)
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium; toast the couscous, stirring, until lightly browned and nutty, ~3-5 min.
Stir in the broth, water, and 1/2 tsp salt; bring to a simmer, then cover and remove from the heat.
Let sit until the liquid is absorbed, ~7 min; fluff with a fork and season.
tips: Toasting the couscous in fat before adding liquid gives nutty flavor and keeps the grains separate and fluffy.
Variation - Carrots, Raisins & Pine Nuts: cook grated carrot in the oil and stir raisins + toasted pine nuts in at the end.
Variation - Dates & Pistachios: fold chopped dates + toasted pistachios in after fluffing.

ingredients: 1 head cauliflower (~2 lb), cut into 1-inch florets
1 red bell pepper, stemmed/seeded, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1 tsp grated lemon zest (+ lemon wedges to serve)
steps: Toss the cauliflower with 3 tbsp oil, salt, and pepper; cook in a skillet until browned and just tender, then set aside.
Add 2 tbsp oil and the bell pepper; cook until softened, then stir in the ras el hanout and garlic until fragrant.
Add the couscous and toast briefly; stir in the broth + lemon zest, cover, and remove from the heat.
Off heat ~7 min, then fluff, fold the cauliflower back in, season, and serve with lemon wedges.
tips: Brown the cauliflower hard for caramelized, nutty flavor; fold it back in at the end so it stays crisp-tender.
Bloom the ras el hanout (catalog p.316) in oil for warm Moroccan depth.

ingredients: 2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tsp grated lemon zest + 3 tbsp juice (about 2 lemons)
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add the potatoes, 1/2 cup water, and 1/2 tsp salt; cover and cook until the edges start to turn translucent.
Reduce to medium-low and cook, covered, until tender, stirring occasionally.
Off heat, whisk the remaining oil with the garlic and lemon zest + juice; toss with the potatoes, finish with parsley, salt, and pepper, and serve.
tips: Covered cooking with a little water then finishing uncovered gives tender insides without deep-frying.
Add the raw garlic + lemon off the heat so they stay bright, not bitter/scorched.
Variation - Olives & Feta: stir in 1/2 cup crumbled feta + 1/4 cup chopped pitted kalamata olives with the parsley.

Roasted Radicchio, Fennel, and Parsnips with Lemon-Basil Sauce

Sauteed Spinach with Yogurt and Dukkah

ingredients: 1 1/2 teaspoons grated lemon zest plus 1 teaspoon juice
steps: Combine yogurt and lemon zest and juice in bowl; set aside for serving. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in Dutch oven over high heat until shimmering. Add spinach 1 handful at a time, stirring and tossing each handful to wilt slightly before adding more. Cook, stirring constantly, until uniformly wilted, about 1 minute. Transfer spinach to colander and squeeze between tongs to release excess liquid.

Wipe pot dry with paper towels. Add remaining 2 tablespoons oil and garlic to now-empty pot and cook over medium heat until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add spinach and toss to coat, gently separating leaves to evenly coat with garlic oil. Off heat, season with salt and pepper. Transfer to serving platter, drizzle with yogurt sauce, and sprinkle with dukkah.
tips: Tagged FAST + VEG. Use CURLY-LEAF spinach — baby spinach wilts down into mush; 2 pounds flat-leaf (about 3 bunches) can substitute.
Squeeze the cooked spinach between tongs in a colander — driving off the excess moisture is what keeps the dish from being watery.
The garlic is toasted in the same pan AFTER the spinach comes out, which turns it sweet and nutty rather than raw.
Dukkah is an Egyptian blend of ground chickpeas, nuts, and spices — ATK prefers their homemade (p.317), but store-bought is a sanctioned substitute.

ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds Swiss chard, stems sliced 1/4 inch thick on bias, leaves sliced into 1/2-inch-wide strips
steps: Heat oil in 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until just shimmering. Add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until lightly browned, 30 to 60 seconds. Add chard stems and 1/8 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until spotty brown and crisp-tender, about 6 minutes.

Add two-thirds of chard leaves and cook, tossing with tongs, until just starting to wilt, 30 to 60 seconds. Add remaining chard leaves and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until leaves are tender, about 3 minutes. Off heat, stir in lemon juice and season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve.
tips: Tagged FAST + VEG. Chard stems fall between spinach's quick stems and kale's tough ribs — slice them thin on the bias and give them a ~6-minute head start with the garlic so they finish with the leaves.
Add the leaves in two stages, first batch wilting before the rest goes in — that's what gives the range of textures.
Lemon juice off-heat at the end keeps the dish bright instead of flat and beety. Any variety of Swiss chard works.

VARIATION - Pancetta & Caramelized Shallots (FAST): omit garlic; brown 3 thinly sliced shallots in 1 tbsp oil 10-12 min; crisp 2 oz pancetta (1/4-inch pieces) in 1 tbsp oil 6-8 min; keep 2 tbsp fat, add 1/8 tsp red pepper flakes with the stems, swap 1 tbsp balsamic for the lemon juice, stir pancetta and shallots in at the end.

VARIATION - Currants & Pine Nuts (FAST, VEG): reduce garlic to 1 clove, add 1/4 tsp ground cumin with it; swap 2 tsp sherry vinegar for the lemon juice and stir in 3 tbsp dried currants + 3 tbsp toasted pine nuts.

ingredients: 2 zucchini, halved lengthwise and sliced 3/4-inch thick
2 red bell peppers, stemmed/seeded, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
steps: Whisk the oil, mustard, rosemary, garlic, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper; reserve half the dressing for serving. Toss the mushrooms, zucchini, and peppers with the rest and thread onto eight 12-inch metal skewers.
Grill the kebabs and the lemon quarters over medium-high, turning, until the vegetables are tender and well browned and the lemons are charred, ~16-18 min.

tips: Make the vegetables the star - meaty portobello + zucchini + bell pepper give varied textures, not just filler.
Grill the lemon quarters: charring mellows and concentrates the juice for the finishing dressing.
Dress lightly before grilling and again after for bold, balanced flavor.

recipes.title: Broiled Bluefish with Preserved Lemon and Zhoug

ingredients: 4 (4- to 6-ounce) skinless bluefish fillets, 1 to 1 1/2 inches thick
1/4 preserved lemon, pulp and white pith removed, rind rinsed and minced (1 tablespoon)
steps: Adjust oven rack 4 inches from broiler element and heat broiler. Pat bluefish dry with paper towels, season with salt and pepper, and place skinned side down in greased rimmed baking sheet.

Combine mayonnaise, preserved lemon, garlic, and sugar in bowl, then spread mixture evenly on tops of fillets. Broil until fish flakes apart when gently prodded with paring knife and registers 140 degrees, about 5 minutes. Serve with Green Zhoug and lemon wedges.
tips: Tagged FAST — two steps, ~5 minutes under the broiler.
Freshness matters most with bluefish: the longer it sits on ice, the fishier it gets. (Mackerel is the book's named substitute.)
The mayonnaise is the glue — it keeps the preserved-lemon coating clinging to the fillets while they cook; the 1/4 teaspoon of sugar speeds the browning under the broiler.
Bluefish's gray-brown flesh turns white when cooked through; the doneness cue is flaking + 140 degrees.
Green Zhoug is a p.316 sub-component (an Israeli hot sauce of fresh herbs and chiles) — homemade or store-bought.
No preserved lemons at the store? The book's own recipe is on p.252.

ingredients: 2 skin-on halibut steaks (1.5 lb each), 1 to 1.5 inches thick, trimmed
steps: For the chermoula: Process cilantro, oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika, salt, and cayenne in a food processor until smooth, about 1 minute, scraping down the sides as needed. Set aside for serving.

For the fish: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 325°F. Pat halibut dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a 12-inch ovensafe nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking. Add halibut and cook until well browned, about 5 minutes.
Gently flip the halibut using two spatulas, then transfer the skillet to the oven. Roast until the halibut flakes apart when prodded with a paring knife and registers 140°F, 6 to 9 minutes.

Carefully transfer halibut to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 5 minutes. Remove the skin and separate each quadrant of meat from the bones by slipping a knife between them. Serve with chermoula.
tips: Halibut steaks are big and delicate — flip them with two spatulas so they do not break apart.
Pull the fish at 140°F for moist, just-cooked meat; overcooking is the main risk with lean halibut.
A 12-inch ovensafe nonstick skillet is essential so the same pan goes from stovetop sear to oven roast.
Swordfish (1 to 1.5 inches thick) can be substituted for the halibut; adjust the oven time as needed.
Chermoula is a bright Moroccan herb sauce — make it first so it is ready the moment the fish comes out.

ingredients: 2 lb skinless swordfish steaks, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 (28-oz) can whole peeled tomatoes, drained (juice reserved) and chopped
steps: Combine the pine nuts, mint, a quarter of the garlic, and the orange zest; set aside for serving.
Cook the onion + celery with salt and pepper ~5 min; add the remaining garlic, thyme, and pepper flakes ~30 sec.
Add the wine and reserved tomato juice and reduce by half (~4 min).
Stir in the tomatoes, clam juice, raisins, and capers; simmer ~15 min to meld.
Pat the swordfish dry, season, nestle in; simmer 4 min, then off heat, cover, and sit 3 min until it flakes.
Serve sprinkled with the pine nut-mint mixture (crusty bread to dip).
tips: Swordfish is meaty and holds its shape - finish it off the heat so it stays just-cooked, not rubbery.
Reduce the wine + tomato juice by half to concentrate the base before adding the rest.
Sicilian sweet-savory balance: raisins + capers + pine nuts. Don't skip the raw pine nut-mint-orange-garlic topping - it brightens the bowl.

recipes.title: Greek-Style Shrimp with Tomatoes and Feta

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb extra-large shrimp (21 to 25 per pound), peeled and deveined
1 red or green bell pepper, stemmed, seeded, and chopped
1 can diced tomatoes (28 oz), drained with 1/2 cup juice reserved
steps: Toss shrimp in a bowl with 1 tablespoon oil, 1 tablespoon ouzo, 1 teaspoon of the garlic, the lemon zest, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon pepper; set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat until shimmering. Add onion, bell pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon salt; cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables release their liquid, 3 to 5 minutes. Uncover and cook until the liquid evaporates and the vegetables soften, about 5 minutes. Stir in the remaining garlic and the pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Stir in the tomatoes and reserved juice, wine, and remaining 2 tablespoons ouzo. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the flavors meld and the sauce is slightly thickened (it should not be completely dry), 5 to 8 minutes. Stir in the parsley and season with salt and pepper to taste.

Reduce heat to medium-low and add the shrimp with any accumulated juices; stir to coat and distribute evenly. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the shrimp are opaque throughout, 6 to 9 minutes, adjusting heat to maintain a bare simmer. Off heat, sprinkle with feta and dill and drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil. Serve.
tips: Toss the shrimp with ouzo, garlic, and lemon zest first — it infuses them with bright anise flavor while you build the sauce.
Cook the shrimp gently right in the sauce over medium-low at a bare simmer (6 to 9 minutes) so they stay tender instead of turning rubbery.
Keep the sauce slightly saucy — do not cook it completely dry.
No ouzo? Substitute Pernod, or vodka plus 1 teaspoon anise seeds.
Serve over steamed white rice and/or with crusty bread to catch the sauce.
